subject.title: feat: expand Carapace component candidates and preview

question: Should Carapace publish the three candidate CSS entry points before two consumers have validated the same interfaces and known selector collisions are resolved?
rationale: Repository policy normally requires shared consumer convergence, while this branch deliberately proposes installable trial surfaces; choosing whether those exports constitute an acceptable experimental contract requires maintainer intent rather than a mechanical code repair.

options.title: Keep candidates preview-only
options.body: Remove the package exports for now, retain the gallery and contract work, and publish each family after two-consumer validation resolves selector and behavior compatibility.

options.title: Sponsor an experimental API
options.body: Keep the exports but explicitly define their instability, versioning, collision policy, and upgrade expectations before release.

options.title: Split the proposal
options.body: Land stable-contract and preview infrastructure separately while holding candidate package APIs for a narrower follow-up decision.

recommendation.title: Keep candidates preview-only
recommendation.body: Remove the package exports for now, retain the gallery and contract work, and publish each family after two-consumer validation resolves selector and behavior compatibility.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the repository member who assembled the candidate architecture and its consumer-readiness evidence, making them the best available owner to frame the intended experimental contract for maintainer approval.
